--- the real repository, as committed ---
Every claim the README states must equal what the tree has. The expensive
one (RESULTS_DIGEST) is skipped unless asked for, and says so rather than
being silently absent.

--- including the digest claim, which runs the suite for real ---
This regenerates fixtures/ and runs test_adversarial.py --digest, then
compares the hash it prints against the one the README's relocation table
records. That table was produced on a different machine, at
/tmp/build_4/..., which no longer exists.

--- a deliberately stale claim must fail ---
stale_demo.py copies the checkable files to a throwaway path, changes ONE
occurrence of ONE number in the copied README, and runs the checker
against the copy. The original tree is not touched. Because the README
states this number twice, changing one occurrence is caught as an
internal disagreement -- the two places no longer agree with each other,
which is the failure this repository keeps hitting.

=== $ python3 stale_demo.py --claim case_count ===
claim under test: case_count
changed ONE occurrence in the copied README: 106 -> 107

case_count          internal_disagreement  readme=106,107 tree=106
empty_dir_count     match                  readme=3 tree=3
fixture_file_count  match                  readme=120 tree=120
grep_test_count     match                  readme=122 tree=122
own_test_count      match                  readme=37 tree=37
results_digest      skipped                needs a real suite run; pass --with-digest
test_count          match                  readme=122 tree=122
failing=1
readmecounts.py exit code: 1
the case_count row, verbatim from the JSON report:
{
 "claim": "case_count",
 "claimed_distinct": [
  "106",
  "107"
 ],
 "measured": "106",
 "state": "internal_disagreement"
}
failing claims: ['case_count']
exit=0

=== $ python3 stale_demo.py --claim test_count ===

--- CLI contract ---
Setup errors are exit 2 and say why on stderr. They must not be confused
with exit 1, which means "a claim did not match".

=== $ python3 readmecounts.py --root /no/such/dir/zzz ===
readmecounts.py: --root is not a directory: /no/such/dir/zzz
exit=2

=== $ python3 readmecounts.py --readme /no/such/file/zzz.md ===
readmecounts.py: could not read /no/such/file/zzz.md: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/no/such/file/zzz.md'
exit=2

=== $ python3 readmecounts.py -o /no/such/dir/zzz/out.json ===
readmecounts.py: could not write --output: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/no/such/dir/zzz/out.json'
exit=2

--- determinism: two runs, byte-identical JSON ---

=== $ python3 readmecounts.py -o /tmp/readmecounts_r1.json --quiet ===
exit=0

=== $ python3 readmecounts.py -o /tmp/readmecounts_r2.json --quiet ===
exit=0

=== $ cmp /tmp/readmecounts_r1.json /tmp/readmecounts_r2.json && echo BYTE_IDENTICAL_two_runs ===
BYTE_IDENTICAL_two_runs
exit=0

=== $ sha256sum /tmp/readmecounts_r1.json /tmp/readmecounts_r2.json ===
61e509e916da414d3dd1cf1e99e46aa15f0b8021f8bd523e102df4248b817348  /tmp/readmecounts_r1.json
61e509e916da414d3dd1cf1e99e46aa15f0b8021f8bd523e102df4248b817348  /tmp/readmecounts_r2.json
exit=0

=== $ rm -f /tmp/readmecounts_r1.json /tmp/readmecounts_r2.json; echo cleaned ===
cleaned
exit=0

--- readmecounts.py leaves the tree as it found it ---
`--with-digest` has to generate fixtures/ to run the suite. Two cases,
both real: one where fixtures/ did not exist, and one where it did and
contained a file that must survive. The second case is here because the
first version of measure_results_digest guarded its own rmtree and then
shelled out to a generator that removes the destination itself -- the
directory, and anything in it, was destroyed.

=== $ test -e fixtures && echo PRESENT || echo ABSENT ===
ABSENT
exit=0

=== $ python3 readmecounts.py --with-digest --quiet; test -e fixtures && echo STILL_THERE || echo fixtures_absent_after ===
fixtures_absent_after
exit=0

=== $ mkdir -p fixtures && printf 'do not delete\n' > fixtures/CANARY.txt && python3 readmecounts.py --with-digest --quiet; cat fixtures/CANARY.txt ===
do not delete
exit=0

=== $ rm -rf fixtures; echo removed_the_canary_dir_this_script_created ===
removed_the_canary_dir_this_script_created
exit=0

--- and the generator itself still verifies clean ---
Run explicitly rather than left to whatever state a previous record
happened to leave behind. The earlier version of this transcript recorded
`make_fixtures.py --verify` AFTER --with-digest had removed fixtures/, so
it captured a VERIFY FAILED (with an absolute build path in it) under a
heading that said "this confirms it verifies clean".

=== $ python3 make_fixtures.py >/dev/null && python3 make_fixtures.py --verify ===
VERIFY OK: 120 files + 3 empty dirs, byte-identical (tree listing and diff -r both agree)
exit=0

=== $ rm -rf fixtures; test -e fixtures && echo STILL_THERE || echo fixtures_removed ===
fixtures_removed
exit=0
